properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 3:59PM MDT until September 15 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern McKinley County in west central New Mexico...

* Until 700 PM MDT.

* At 359 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.75 and 1.25 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.75 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southern McKinley County.

Flash flooding can be expected along Highway 36, Knife Hill Canyon
Road and Indian Reservation Road 9. Elevated water flows are also
expected in the Rio Pescado.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.areaDesc: Rio Arriba, NM; Santa Fe, NM
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 3:48PM MDT until September 15 at 6:45PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Frijoles burn scar in...
Southeastern Rio Arriba County in north central New Mexico...
Northeastern Santa Fe County in north central New Mexico...

* Until 645 PM MDT.

* At 348 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the western portion of the Frijoles Burn Scar as
well as areas west of the burn scar to including Cundiyo. Between
0.25 and 0.75 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall
amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned area. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact the Rio Frijoles,
Rio Medio and Chimayo Creek as well as Camino del Canon, County Road
127 and Camino del Molino. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials. Flooding will also impact
Cundiyo and Highway 503.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Frijoles Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Frijoles Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Chimayo, Cundiyo, Rio Chiquito, Nambe Pueblo, Nambe Lake and
Cordova.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the Frijoles Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 6:45 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 6:45 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 15 at 3:15PM MDT until September 15 at 4:45PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
At 315 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated up to 0.75 inches of rain fell
across Buckskin Gulch, Wire Pass, and the Wave. Although
thunderstorms have moved away from the area, flash flooding likely
ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks, streams, slot
canyons, and normally dry washes.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Buckskin Gulch, Wire Pass, and the Wave.

This includes US Route 89 between mile markers 14 and 27.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.
